mainTopic: Whether doing a מצוה affects liability (impurity from a מת מצוה, the עומר harvest, a father who strikes his son), and who goes into גלות for killing whom.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion between רבא and רבינא. A person made impure by a מת מצוה is still liable for entering the מקדש, and the source is the extra word 'עוד' in the פסוק. A second version places the discussion on a ברייתא about 'בחריש ובקציר תשבת'. There, רבי ישמעאל teaches that only optional harvesting is forbidden on שבת, so harvesting the עומר, which is a מצוה, is allowed. רבא first proves that plowing is never a מצוה, defends this against a challenge from a father who disciplines his son, and then switches to a stronger proof from comparing harvesting to plowing. A new משנה follows, explaining who goes into גלות for accidentally killing whom: father and son, Jews and others, and a גר תושב. The גמרא narrows the case of a father who is exiled until it reaches a son learning carpentry who already knows another trade. For a son who kills his father, רב כהנא says the sources follow רבי שמעון and the רבנן, while רבא says the ברייתא excludes only accidental wounding. Finally, the גמרא asks why a Jew would get lashes because of a כותי or an עבד. After the answer about an עד זומם fails, רב אחא בריה דרב איקא begins to explain it as a case of striking, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Impure in any case
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the words 'טמא יהיה' teach that a person who enters the מקדש while impure is liable no matter how he became impure, even through a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He shall be impure' (במדבר 19:13) means: in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: We join the conversation mid-answer. The question was whether someone made impure by burying a מת מצוה is exempt from punishment for entering the מקדש, and the answer is no: 'טמא יהיה' covers every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that becoming impure through a מצוה should protect a person from liability. The answer reads 'יהיה' ('he shall be') as covering every kind of impurity, whatever its cause. So the מצוה behind the impurity does not remove the punishment of כרת for entering the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case; no matter how it happened
An unattended dead body that everyone must bury, even a כהן
Ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: This line is an answer to a question asked just before this section begins. The question was whether a person made impure by a מת מצוה is liable for entering the מקדש.

phrases.english: "He shall be impure" – in any case.
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:13. However he became impure, even through a מצוה, makes no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section about impurity caused by a מת מצוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'טמא יהיה' make the liability apply in every case of impurity, including impurity from a מצוה.

steps.title: Those words are already used for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'טמא יהיה' is already needed for a ברייתא that includes a טבול יום, and 'טומאתו בו' is needed to include a מחוסר כיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'He shall be impure' comes to include a טבול יום, and 'his impurity is upon him' comes to include a מחוסר כיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source just given. It says 'טמא יהיה' is already 'taken' by a different teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא uses 'טמא יהיה' to teach that a טבול יום who enters the מקדש is liable. If the phrase is used up for that teaching, it cannot also be the source for impurity from a מת מצוה. The same ברייתא uses 'טומאתו בו' for a מחוסר כיפורים, so that part of the פסוק is also taken.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
To include
Someone who went to the מקוה today but must wait until nightfall to be fully pure
Someone who still has to bring his atonement offering to finish becoming pure

phrases.english: He needs that for what was taught in a ברייתא:
"He shall be impure" – to include one who immersed that day;
"His impurity is upon him" – to include one lacking atonement!
phrases.notes: For example, a זב or a מצורע who has immersed but hasn't brought his קרבן yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'טמא יהיה' as the source for liability when the impurity came from a מת מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One phrase cannot teach two separate rules, and this phrase is already used for the טבול יום.

steps.title: The source is the word 'עוד'
steps.stepSummary: He answers that the real source is the extra word 'עוד' in the phrase 'עוד טומאתו בו', not 'טמא יהיה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I was speaking about 'his impurity is yet [upon him]'.
steps.whatsHappening: The source is moved to a different word in the same פסוק. That word is free to teach this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'טמא יהיה' and 'טומאתו בו' are used for the טבול יום and the מחוסר כיפורים. The extra word 'עוד' is not used for anything, so it teaches that a person is liable however he became impure. That includes impurity from a מת מצוה, so the conclusion of step 1 stands with a better source.

keyTerms.meaning: Yet; still. Here it is an extra word that teaches an added rule
I was saying; I meant

steps.whatToRemember: A person made impure by a מת מצוה is still liable for entering the מקדש. The source is the extra word 'עוד' in 'עוד טומאתו בו'.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I was speaking from "his impurity is yet [upon him]".
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, במדבר 19:13. The extra word 'עוד' is the real source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by pointing to a different word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the source to a different word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule was being learned from 'טמא יהיה', which is already used for the טבול יום.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from the extra word 'עוד', which is not needed for anything else.

steps.title: Another version: the plowing and harvest ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some teach this discussion on a different ברייתא. In it, רבי עקיבא says the פסוק 'בחריש ובקציר תשבת' adds plowing just before שביעית and harvesting just after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on this: 'In plowing and in harvest you shall rest.' רבי עקיבא says: The פסוק does not need to tell us about plowing and harvesting in שביעית, since it already says 'Your field you shall not sow and your vineyard you shall not prune.' Rather, it teaches even plowing on the eve of שביעית that helps the seventh year, and harvesting of seventh-year crops that continues after שביעית ends.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where this discussion took place. It starts by bringing the ברייתא the discussion is built on, beginning with רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק as being about שביעית. Plowing and harvesting in שביעית itself are already forbidden by another פסוק, so this פסוק must add something new. It adds time at both edges: plowing before שביעית that helps the seventh year's crops, and harvesting seventh-year crops after the year is over.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach this discussion on a different source
The seventh year, when farming the land is forbidden
It does not need to say (this is already known)
The end of the sixth year, just before שביעית
The time right after שביעית ends

steps.confusionAlert: In רבי עקיבא's view this פסוק is about שביעית, not שבת.

phrases.english: Some teach it on this:
phrases.notes: The same discussion between רבא and רבינא, but tied to the ברייתא that comes next.

phrases.english: "In plowing and in harvest you shall rest";
phrases.notes: שמות 34:21

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
It does not need to say

phrases.aramaic: חָרִישׁ שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית וְקָצִיר שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: plowing of the seventh year and harvest of the seventh year,
since it has already been stated:
"Your field you shall not sow and your vineyard you shall not prune";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:4

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ חָרִישׁ שֶׁל עֶרֶב שְׁבִיעִית
phrases.english: rather, even plowing on the eve of the seventh year
that goes into the seventh year,
phrases.notes: Plowing done before שביעית whose benefit carries into the seventh year.

phrases.english: and harvest of the seventh year
that goes out into the year after the seventh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the same discussion, built on a different ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the פסוק forbids plowing before שביעית that helps the seventh year, and harvesting seventh-year crops after the year ends.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: only optional harvesting is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל compares harvesting to plowing. Just as plowing is optional, the forbidden harvesting is optional harvesting, so the harvest of the עומר, which is a מצוה, is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: Just as plowing is optional, so too the harvest is optional. This leaves out the harvest of the עומר, which is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives his reading of the same פסוק. This sets up the second version of the discussion: a rule that a מצוה is left out of a ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי עקיבא, רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק as being about plowing and harvesting on שבת. Plowing is never a מצוה, so by comparison the harvest the פסוק forbids is only optional harvesting. The harvest of the עומר is a מצוה, so it is allowed on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Optional; not a מצוה
Just as ... so too (a comparison)
Cutting the barley for the עומר offering, which is a מצוה
Is left out; is excluded

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same kind of reasoning used in the first version: something done as a מצוה is treated differently from something done by choice. That is why this ברייתא can serve as the base for the second version.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
Just as plowing is optional,
so too the harvest is optional.
This excludes the harvest of the עומר, which is a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי ישמעאל אומר מה חריש רשות אף קציר רשות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the same ברייתא, disagreeing with רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The forbidden harvest is only optional harvesting, so harvesting the עומר, which is a מצוה, is permitted.

steps.title: Maybe the plowing in the פסוק is plowing for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A scholar asks רבא how we know the forbidden plowing is optional. Perhaps it means plowing for the עומר, which is a מצוה, and the Torah still says to rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the scholars said to רבא: How do we know the plowing is optional plowing? Maybe it is plowing for the עומר, which is a מצוה, and even so the Torah said 'rest'!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the base of רבי ישמעאל's comparison from Step 5. He asks why we assume the plowing is optional at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל said that harvesting is like plowing, and plowing is optional, so the harvest of the עומר is not included. The scholar attacks the first half of that argument. If the plowing could be for the עומר, then the comparison would prove the opposite: even work done for a מצוה would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Plowing
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
Literally 'the Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
You shall rest (stop working)

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Rava:
From where do we know that the plowing is optional plowing?
Perhaps it is plowing for the omer, which is a מצוה,
phrases.notes: He means plowing a field to grow the barley for the עומר offering.

phrases.english: and even so the Torah says: "You shall rest"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רבי ישמעאל's comparison in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's assumption that the plowing in the פסוק is optional.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plowing for the עומר serves a מצוה, so the פסוק might forbid even work done for a מצוה. That would ruin the comparison.

steps.title: Plowing is never a מצוה in itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that if a field is already plowed, you don't need to plow it. So plowing itself is not a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since if he finds the field already plowed he does not plow it, plowing is not a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רבי ישמעאל. Even plowing for the עומר does not count as a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real מצוה is something you must do yourself. With plowing, if the field is already plowed you just go ahead and plant. So plowing is only a preparation, which means all plowing counts as optional.

keyTerms.meaning: Already plowed
Since, because

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֵּיוָן דְּאִם מָצָא חָרוּשׁ
phrases.english: He said to him: Since if he found the field already plowed
he does not plow it, it is not a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what counts as a מצוה: only something that must be done even when it is already done.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plowing for the עומר is a מצוה, so the פסוק forbids even work for a מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plowing is only a preparation and never a מצוה in itself, so the plowing in the פסוק is optional.

steps.title: Challenge from a father who hits his son
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points out that the משנה calls a father hitting his son a מצוה. By רבא's test it should not be one, since a son who is already learned does not need hitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected to רבא: The משנה excludes from exile a father who hits his son, a teacher who disciplines his student, and a messenger of בית דין. But why? Let us say: since if the son were already learned it would not be a מצוה, now too it is not a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tests רבא's rule on another case. He uses the earlier משנה that says people who kill while doing a מצוה don't go into גלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts a father who hits his son because it is a מצוה. But by רבא's test, hitting is only a tool for teaching. If the son were already learned there would be no need, so it should not count as a מצוה, and the father should go into גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Who disciplines or keeps in line
A messenger of the court who gives lashes
Already learned
But why?

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection to Rava:
Excluded is the father who strikes his son,
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the earlier משנה, which exempts these people from גלות if they kill by accident.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרַב הָרוֹדֶה אֶת תַּלְמִידוֹ, וּשְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and the teacher who disciplines his student, and the agent of the court.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַמַּאי? לֵימָא כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ גְּמִיר לָאו מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: But why? Let us say: since if the son were learned it would not be a מצוה,
now too it is not a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's test from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that something unnecessary when already done is not a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hitting a son is unnecessary once he is learned, yet the משנה treats it as a מצוה. That contradicts רבא's rule.

steps.title: Disciplining a son is a מצוה even when he is learned
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that disciplining a son is a מצוה even if he is learned, based on the פסוק 'יסר בנך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, even if the son is learned, the father is still doing a מצוה, as it says: 'Discipline your son and he will give you rest.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows that the father's case does not break his rule. Discipline is a מצוה at all times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes disciplining one's son a מצוה in itself, not only a tool for teaching. So even a learned son is included, and the case passes רבא's test. Plowing has no such פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that case
Discipline your son and he will give you rest

phrases.english: There, even though the son is learned,
he is still performing a מצוה,
as it is written: "Chastise your son, and he will give you rest."
phrases.notes: משלי 29:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: a פסוק makes discipline a מצוה in itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hitting a son is only a tool for teaching, so it fails רבא's test.
steps.terutzMaskana: Disciplining a son is a מצוה even when he is learned, so the rule still stands.

steps.title: רבא gives a new reason: harvesting is compared to plowing
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops his first reasoning. Harvesting is compared to plowing: plowing is skipped if already done, so the forbidden harvesting is also one that is skipped if already done. The עומר harvest is a מצוה even if cut grain is available, so it is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: What I said is nothing. Harvesting is like plowing. Just as with plowing, if he finds the field plowed he does not plow, so too with harvesting, if he finds it harvested he does not harvest. And if you think it means a מצוה harvest, would he not harvest if he found it harvested? It is a מצוה to harvest and bring!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes back his first answer to the question of Step 6. He gives a new and stronger proof that the פסוק means optional work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the proof comes from the harvesting side. The פסוק joins the two, so the forbidden harvesting must be like plowing, which is skipped when already done. But the עומר must be freshly harvested as a מצוה even if cut grain is already there. So the עומר harvest cannot be what the פסוק forbids, and the פסוק must be talking about optional work.

keyTerms.meaning: It is nothing, it is not a good argument
Harvesting
Similar to, compared to
If it enters your mind, if you think

steps.whatToRemember: The final reason: harvesting is compared to plowing. The עומר harvest is a מצוה you must do even if cut grain is ready, so it does not fit the comparison. According to רבי ישמעאל, it is not included in the ban on harvesting on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking back the result. He still holds that the פסוק forbids only optional work. He is only swapping his reason for a better one.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי.
phrases.english: Rava then said: What I said is nothing.
Harvesting is similar to plowing:

phrases.aramaic: מָה חֲרִישָׁה, מָצָא חָרוּשׁ – אֵינוֹ חוֹרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: just as with plowing, if he found it plowed he does not plow,

phrases.aramaic: אַף קְצִירָה נָמֵי, מָצָא קָצוּר אֵינוֹ קוֹצֵר,
phrases.english: so too with harvesting, if he found it harvested he does not harvest.
And if it enters your mind that it means a מצוה harvest,
would he really not harvest if he found it harvested?!
It is a מצוה to harvest and bring!
phrases.notes: He means the barley for the עומר, which must be cut fresh for the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's first answer (Step 7) with a new answer to the question of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New proof from the comparison of harvesting to plowing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plowing in the פסוק might be plowing for the עומר, a מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden harvesting must be skippable like plowing. The עומר harvest is not skippable, so the פסוק speaks only of optional work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the line that began with Step 5: according to רבי ישמעאל, the harvest of the עומר is allowed even on שבת, because the פסוק forbids only optional work.

steps.title: New משנה: who goes into exile for killing whom
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a father goes into גלות for killing his son and a son for killing his father. Everyone goes into גלות for killing a Jew and a Jew for killing them, except a גר תושב, who goes into גלות only for killing another גר תושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A father goes into exile because of his son, and a son because of his father. Everyone goes into exile because of a Jew, and a Jew goes into exile because of them, except for a גר תושב. A גר תושב goes into exile only because of another גר תושב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists which accidental killers go to a city of refuge, depending on who the victim was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that family ties do not cancel גלות. A father or son who kills the other by accident still goes. It also sets the limits of the rule: killing a גר תושב, or a גר תושב killing a Jew, is not handled by גלות, but one גר תושב killing another is.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Goes into exile to a city of refuge
Because of, for killing
A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who keeps the seven מצוות of בני נח

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The father is exiled due to the son,
and the son is exiled due to the father.
Everyone is exiled due to a Jew,
and Jews are exiled due to them,
except for a ger toshav.
And a ger toshav is not exiled
except due to a ger toshav.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאָב גּוֹלֶה עַל יְדֵי הַבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father and son go into גלות for killing each other. Everyone and Jews go into גלות for killing one another, except a גר תושב, who goes into גלות only for killing another גר תושב.

steps.title: How can a father be exiled for killing his son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a father goes into גלות for killing his son. It points out that the earlier משנה said a father who hits his son is not exiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a father goes into גלות because of his son. But didn't you say: a father who hits his son is excluded?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting our משנה and immediately points out a contradiction with the earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said that a father who hits his son and kills him by accident does not go into גלות, because hitting is a מצוה. So how can our משנה say a father is exiled for killing his son?

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here
But didn't you say? (pointing to a contradiction)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ הָאָב גּוֹלֶה עַל יְדֵי הַבֵּן.
phrases.english: GEMARA: The father is exiled because of the son.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ: יָצָא הָאָב הַמַּכֶּה אֶת בְּנוֹ!
phrases.english: But didn't you say: excluded is a father who hits his son!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ: יָצָא הָאָב הַמַּכֶּה אֶת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 11 using the earlier משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a father is exiled for killing his son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier משנה exempts a father who hits his son, so a father should not be exiled for killing his son

steps.title: The son was already learned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a son who is already learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a son who is learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה is talking about a son who has already learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that hitting a son who already knows his learning is not needed. So it is not a מצוה, and the father who kills him by accident is exiled.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is learned / who has already learned

phrases.english: Where he is learned.
phrases.notes: The son has already learned, so there was no reason to hit him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by limiting the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father is hitting as part of the מצוה of teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: The son is learned, so the hitting is not a מצוה and the father is exiled

steps.title: Even a learned son may be disciplined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reminds us that רבא already said disciplining a son is a מצוה even if he is learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say that even if he is learned, the father is doing a מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer, because of what was said in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 רבא said, based on 'יסר בנך', that hitting a son is a מצוה even if he is learned. So the answer 'he is learned' does not take away the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
He is doing a מצוה

phrases.english: Didn't you say that even though he is learned
phrases.notes: This points back to רבא's answer from 'יסר בנך' in step 9.

phrases.english: he is doing a מצוה!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמְרַתְּ אַף עַל גַּב דִּגְמִיר מִצְוָה קָעָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the son was learned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Disciplining a son is a מצוה even when he is learned, so the father should still be exempt

steps.title: A carpenter's apprentice
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a son who is learning carpentry from his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a carpenter's apprentice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case: the father hit his son while teaching him carpentry, not Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of disciplining is about learning Torah. When the father is teaching a trade, the hitting is not that מצוה, so the father is exiled.

keyTerms.meaning: Apprentice
Carpenters

phrases.english: With a carpenter's apprentice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 with a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father was hitting to teach Torah
steps.terutzMaskana: The father was teaching carpentry, which is not the מצוה of disciplining for Torah

steps.title: Teaching a trade is also a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that teaching a son a trade gives him a livelihood, so it is also a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A carpenter's apprentice: it is his livelihood that he is teaching him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: teaching a son how to earn a living is itself a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If teaching a trade is a מצוה, then hitting the son while teaching him is also part of a מצוה. So the father should again be exempt from גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Livelihood, a way to make a living
That he is teaching him

phrases.english: A carpenter's apprentice:
it is his livelihood that he is teaching him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Teaching a livelihood is a מצוה, so hitting during it is part of a מצוה

steps.title: He already knows another trade
steps.stepSummary: The son already learned a different trade, so teaching him carpentry is not a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he has already learned another trade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the son already has a trade to live from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the son can already earn a living, teaching him a second trade is not a מצוה. So the hitting is optional, and the father who kills him by accident goes into גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: A trade, a craft
Another, a different one

steps.whatToRemember: A father is exiled for killing his son only when the hitting was not a מצוה at all: a son learning carpentry who already knows another trade.

phrases.english: Where he has learned another trade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by narrowing the case even more
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Teaching carpentry is teaching him a livelihood, which is a מצוה
steps.terutzMaskana: He already has a trade, so the second trade is not a מצוה and the father is exiled

steps.title: A ברייתא says one who strikes his father is excluded
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a son is exiled for killing his father, but a ברייתא learns from the פסוק that one who strikes his father is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the son is exiled because of the father.' But there is a contradiction: 'one who strikes a person', to exclude one who strikes his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the משנה and shows a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a son who kills his father by accident goes into גלות. The ברייתא reads the words 'מכה נפש' as leaving out one who strikes his father, so he does not go into גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: And there is a contradiction (between two sources)
One who strikes a person
To exclude, to leave out

phrases.aramaic: וְהַבֵּן גּוֹלֶה עַל יְדֵי הָאָב כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: And the son is exiled because of the father, etc.
And there is a contradiction: 'one who strikes a person'
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:11

phrases.english: to exclude one who strikes his father.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי מַכֵּה נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָט לַמַּכָּה אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the second rule of the משנה quoted in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a son is exiled for killing his father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reads the פסוק as excluding one who strikes his father from גלות

steps.title: Two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון and the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It is not difficult. This one is רבי שמעון, and that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא settles the contradiction by saying the two sources follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that excludes a son follows רבי שמעון. Our משנה, which says the son is exiled, follows the רבנן. The next step explains why רבי שמעון holds this way.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one ... and that one (matching each source to an opinion)
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: It is not difficult;
this is Rabbi Shimon and that is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא goes with רבי שמעון; our משנה goes with the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different opinions (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source follows a different opinion: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון and the משנה follows the רבנן

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reasoning: חנק is more severe
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, חנק is more severe than סייף. An accidental sin of a סייף kind can be atoned for, but an accidental sin of a חנק kind cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, who says חנק is more severe than סייף: the accidental version of a סייף sin was given atonement, the accidental version of a חנק sin was not given atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why, for רבי שמעון, a son who kills his father by accident does not go into גלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular murderer is punished with סייף, and for רבי שמעון someone who kills his father is punished with חנק, which he holds is more severe. גלות is an atonement for the accidental version of a סייף sin. A sin in the more severe חנק group is too serious for גלות to atone, so the son is not exiled.

keyTerms.meaning: Death by strangulation
Death by the sword
More severe
An accidental sin
Atonement

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a more severe sin means more punishment here. For רבי שמעון, the sin is so serious that גלות cannot atone for it, so the son does not go into גלות at all.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, who says
strangulation is more severe than the sword,
the accidental version of a sword sin was given atonement,
phrases.notes: He means an ordinary murder, which is punished by the sword when done on purpose.

phrases.english: the accidental version of a strangulation sin was not given atonement.
phrases.notes: Killing a father falls in this group for רבי שמעון, so גלות does not atone for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר חֶנֶק חָמוּר מִסַּיִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב כהנא's answer in step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reasoning of one side
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is unclear why רבי שמעון would exclude a son from גלות
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, killing a father belongs in the more severe חנק group, and גלות cannot atone for that kind of accidental sin

steps.title: For the רבנן, accidentally killing a father can be atoned for by exile
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא finishes his answer. The רבנן hold that סייף is harsher than חנק, so a son who accidentally kills his father has made a סייף-type mistake. That kind of mistake can be atoned for by exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, who say סייף is more severe than חנק, one who kills his father by accident has made a סייף-type mistake, and a סייף-type mistake can be atoned for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב כהנא's answer. It shows why the משנה, which follows the רבנן, says a son who kills his father is exiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, רבי שמעון said חנק is the harsher death, so a son who kills his father commits a חנק-type sin, and exile cannot atone for it. The רבנן say the opposite: סייף is harsher. So the son's killing counts as a סייף-type sin, and exile can atone for that. This explains why the משנה and the ברייתא disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Can be atoned for (here, by going to exile)
By accident, without intending it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון says חנק is harsher, so the son is not exiled. The רבנן say סייף is harsher, so the son is exiled. This is רב כהנא's way of explaining why the משנה and the ברייתא disagree.

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis, who say
execution by sword is more severe than strangulation,
one who kills his father [unintentionally]
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: it is an accidental sin of the sword type,
and an accidental sin of the sword type can be atoned for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב כהנא's answer by giving the רבנן's side, the mirror image of רבי שמעון's view in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different tannaim: the משנה follows the רבנן and the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to contradict each other about a son who kills his father.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the רבנן, the son's killing is a סייף-type sin, which exile can atone for, so the משנה exiles him.

steps.title: רבא: the exclusion is about accidentally wounding a father
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently. The ברייתא's exclusion is not about killing a father. It is about a son who accidentally wounds his father, and that son is not exiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the exclusion is for one who wounds his father by accident. You might have thought that since doing it on purpose carries the death penalty, doing it by accident should mean exile. So the פסוק teaches us that he is not exiled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the contradiction from Step 18. He explains that the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about different cases, so there is no argument between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says everyone agrees that a son who accidentally kills his father is exiled. The ברייתא is excluding a son who accidentally wounds his father. We might have thought he goes to exile, since wounding a father on purpose is punished by death, just like murder. The ברייתא teaches that exile applies only to accidental killing.

keyTerms.meaning: A wound that draws blood or leaves a bruise
On purpose
Someone who deserves the death penalty
You might have thought (introduces the mistaken first idea)
It teaches us (introduces the real lesson)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not disagree with the משנה. In his view, a son who accidentally kills his father is exiled according to everyone. Only accidental wounding is excluded.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that exile is only for accidental killing. It is not for other accidental acts, even acts that carry the death penalty when done on purpose.

phrases.english: Rava says:
to exclude one who inflicts a wound
on his father unintentionally.
It would enter your mind to say:
since if done intentionally he is liable to death,
if done unintentionally let him also be exiled,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: פְּרָט לְעוֹשֶׂה חַבּוּרָה בְּאָבִיו בְּשׁוֹגֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of רב כהנא's answer that two tannaim disagree, רבא says the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about different cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: killing in the משנה, wounding in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since wounding a father on purpose is a capital crime, wounding him by accident might call for exile.
steps.terutzMaskana: Exile is only for accidental killing. A son who accidentally wounds his father is not exiled, and a son who accidentally kills him is exiled.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' in the משנה add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'everyone is exiled for killing a Jew' and asks which extra people the word 'everyone' is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: everyone is exiled for killing a Jew, etc. 'Everyone is exiled for killing a Jew': what does this add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It asks which case 'everyone' adds, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word like 'everyone' suggests there is a case we would not have known about otherwise. The גמרא wants to know which people are being added.

keyTerms.meaning: Are exiled (sent to a city of refuge)
What does it come to include?

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל גּוֹלִין עַל יְדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The mishna says: Everyone is exiled due to a Jew, etc.
"Everyone is exiled due to a Jew":
what does it come to add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the father-son topic and starts on the next line of the משנה.

steps.title: It adds an עבד and a כותי
steps.stepSummary: The word 'everyone' comes to include a Canaanite slave (עבד) and a כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to add a slave and a Samaritan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: 'everyone' includes an עבד and a כותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this word, we might have thought that an עבד or a כותי is not part of the exile system. The משנה teaches that they are also exiled for accidentally killing a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: A Canaanite slave
A Samaritan, whose conversion and observance were questioned

phrases.english: To add a slave and a Samaritan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Everyone' includes an עבד and a כותי.

steps.title: The משנה matches a ברייתא about עבד and כותי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה already teaches what a ברייתא says outright: an עבד or a כותי is exiled and given lashes because of a Jew, and a Jew is exiled and given lashes because of a כותי or an עבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have already learned in the משנה what the רבנן taught: a slave or a Samaritan is exiled and lashed because of a Jew, and a Jew is exiled and lashed because of a Samaritan or a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the משנה to a ברייתא that says the same thing more fully. This also sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא works in both directions and adds lashes as well as exile. Exile is for accidentally killing. Lashes are for an act that carries a punishment of lashes, which the next step says is cursing.

keyTerms.meaning: Receives lashes (flogging)

phrases.english: We have learned in our mishna that which the Rabbis taught:
A slave and a Samaritan are exiled and flogged
due to a Jew,
and a Jew is exiled and flogged
due to a Samaritan and a slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in Step 24 matches an explicit ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's word 'everyone' includes an עבד and a כותי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of תנו רבנן that says this explicitly, in both directions.

steps.title: Why would a Jew get lashes for cursing a כותי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts most of the ברייתא but questions one part. A Jew who kills a כותי by accident is exiled, but why would he get lashes for cursing him? The ban on cursing protects only someone who acts like a proper member of 'your people.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that a slave or a Samaritan is exiled and lashed because of a Jew: exiled for killing him, lashed for cursing him. But a Jew exiled and lashed because of a Samaritan? Exile makes sense, for killing him. But lashes, why? For cursing him? The פסוק says: 'A leader among your people you shall not curse,' which means one who acts the way your people act!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the ברייתא. It accepts everything except one point: a Jew getting lashes for cursing a כותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exile for accidental killing works in every direction. Lashes for cursing are based on the פסוק 'בעמך,' which protects only someone who behaves like a Torah-observant Jew. Since a כותי does not act that way, cursing him should not bring lashes, so the ברייתא seems hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (accepts one part before challenging another)
Because he cursed him
A leader
One who acts as your people act, meaning he keeps the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The question is only about lashes. The גמרא fully accepts that a Jew is exiled for accidentally killing a כותי.

phrases.english: Granted, a slave and a Samaritan
are exiled and flogged due to a Jew:
exiled, where he killed him;
and flogged, where he cursed him.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹלֶה וְלוֹקֶה עַל יְדֵי כּוּתִי?
phrases.english: But a Jew exiled and flogged due to a Samaritan?
Granted, exiled, where he killed him;
but flogged, for what?
Because he cursed him?
"And a leader among your people you shall not curse"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:27

phrases.english: refers to one who acts as your people act!
phrases.notes: The word 'בעמך,' 'among your people,' is read as limiting the ban to someone who behaves like a Torah-observant Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹלֶה וְלוֹקֶה עַל יְדֵי כּוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the ברייתא quoted in Step 25 and challenges its rule about lashes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a Jew gets lashes because of a כותי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lashes would be for cursing, but the ban on cursing ('בעמך') protects only someone who acts like 'your people,' and a כותי does not. So there should be no lashes.

steps.title: The lashes are for being a lying witness
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that the lashes in the ברייתא are not for cursing. They are for testifying against the other person and being caught as an עד זומם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב said: The case is where one testified against the other and was proven a lying witness (הוזם).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the question from step 26 with a different kind of lashes. The ברייתא is talking about lashes given to עדים זוממין, not lashes for cursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the ban on cursing does not protect a כותי, so cursing him should not bring lashes. רב אחא moves the lashes to a completely different sin, lying in court. Lying testimony against anyone can bring a punishment, whoever the victim is.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier idea (lashes for cursing) is being dropped for a new explanation.
He testified against him
He was proven a lying witness by other witnesses who say he was somewhere else at the time
Lying witnesses who are punished with the punishment they tried to bring on the other person

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
For example, where he testified against him and was proven a lying witness.
phrases.notes: So the lashes in the ברייתא come from lying in court, not from cursing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26 by switching the source of the lashes from cursing to false testimony.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the lashes come from a different sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lashes in the ברייתא are for cursing, which does not fit a כותי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lashes are for being an עד זומם who testified against the other person.

steps.title: A slave cannot be a witness at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב. The ברייתא also has an עבד getting lashes because of a Jew. An עבד cannot testify, so he can never become an עד זומם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same case applied to a slave would mean he testified against a Jew and was proven a lying witness. But is a slave fit to give testimony?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב אחא's answer on the עבד from the same ברייתא, and it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the עבד and the כותי together, so one explanation should fit both. An עבד is not a valid witness, so his testimony is not real testimony. Without real testimony there is no הזמה and no lashes, so רב אחא's explanation fails for the עבד.

keyTerms.meaning: The same kind of case, the matching case
A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew
Someone fit to be a witness

phrases.english: The same case regarding a slave,
where he testified against him and was proven a lying witness,
is a slave fit to give testimony?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 27 by applying it to the עבד in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's explanation that the lashes are for being an עד זומם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The explanation must also fit the עבד, but an עבד is not a valid witness, so he can never be punished as an עד זומם.

steps.title: The case is where one struck the other
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא gives a new explanation. The lashes in the ברייתא are for one person hitting the other with a blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא the son of רב איקא said: What case are we dealing with here? Where one struck the other with a blow...
steps.whatsHappening: After the עד זומם answer failed, a new אמורא explains the ברייתא as a case of hitting. Anyone can hit, including an עבד, a כותי, or a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer avoids both problems. It is not about cursing, so it does not matter whether the כותי counts as 'your people.' It is not about testimony, so it does not matter that an עבד cannot be a witness. The sentence continues in the next part of the daf, where the גמרא describes this blow more exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? It introduces a narrower case that solves the problem.
A blow, a hit

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. The גמרא goes on to describe what kind of blow this is.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he struck him with a blow

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 27 with a new case that works for both the עבד and the כותי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the lashes are for striking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lashes come from cursing or from false testimony, and neither fits both the כותי and the עבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lashes come from one person striking the other, which can apply to everyone in the ברייתא.
